close_reason:
Fixed in c7ba657. MemoryBackend.create_object now enforces RFC 9610 §2 at-most-one-default invariant for AddressBook (parallel to the update-side fix in bd:JMAP-qz9v.11). When a create makes a new book default, all previously-default sibling books in the same account are demoted in the same critical section. Demoted ids are recorded in the change_log so AddressBook/changes surfaces them per RFC 8620 §5.2.

Two new integration tests on MemoryBackend exercise: create-with-isDefault demotes existing default, demoted id appears in /changes updated.

Handler-side concern (not landing here): the handler does NOT re-fetch demoted siblings into the wire 'updated' map of the /set response on the regular create/update paths. Today only the onSuccessSetIsDefault block does this re-fetch. Tracked at bd:JMAP-qz9v.57.

Side note: RFC 9610 §2 marks isDefault as '(server-set)', which per RFC 8620 §1.6 would mean clients MUST NOT send it on create. Workspace currently allows client-supplied isDefault on create (test fixtures rely on it). The strict-server-set reading is a separate design call independent of this fix; the invariant enforcement above satisfies the MUST NOT-more-than-one half of §2 regardless. 94+33+1 tests pass; workspace clean.
description:
Trigger: AddressBook/set create with {c1: {name: 'X', isDefault: true}} while an existing default book ('book1', isDefault: true) is already in the account.

Bad behavior: handle_address_book_set (addressbook.rs:107-183) calls backend.create_object verbatim with the created object. MemoryBackend.create_object (memory.rs:602-644) just serializes-and-stores the object with no single-default enforcement. The onSuccessSetIsDefault path DOES demote other books (handler lines 354-372, plus MockBackend.update_object's special case at lib.rs:427-435), but plain create with isDefault: true does NOT.

After the call, the account has two AddressBooks both with isDefault: true. RFC 9610 §2 doesn't say isDefault MUST be unique, but RFC 9610 §2.3's 'onSuccessSetIsDefault' machinery and the §4.2 example (where setting one default clears the other) imply 'at most one default' as an invariant.

Note: this matches workspace pattern 'backends are canonical for permission enforcement' — the handler legitimately delegates to the backend, and a real backend would atomically maintain the invariant. So the bug is split:
 - MemoryBackend does not maintain the invariant (P1 — it's a reference impl).
 - The handler does not re-fetch other books after a successful create-with-isDefault and report demoted ones in updated, the way it does for onSuccessSetIsDefault (P1 — implementors will copy this pattern as-is).

If 'at most one default' is intentionally relaxed in this workspace, the implication should be documented in PLAN.md and README; today it's implicit and inconsistent with the §4.2 spec example shape.
title: AddressBook/set create does not enforce single-default invariant for newly created default AddressBook
